title: Climb the levels
summary: Let the population move up from empty streets on its own, fairly, in more than one city.

steps.title: One level at a time
steps.body:
Rush hour is far too hard to learn from scratch. A curriculum starts easy and moves on once the population is ready, like a driving school.

`autoLevel(share: 20%)` moves up a level once a fifth of the best brains' trips arrive safely, averaged over a few generations. Press Check to train 25 generations and see the highest level they reach.
hints: The call goes inside each generation.

steps.title: More than one trip
steps.body:
One trip a generation is a lottery. A brain that happened to get an easy route looks better than it is, and the curriculum can move on by luck.

`routesPerGeneration` has every brain drive the same few trips one after another and adds up its fitness. Ask for 2. More trips are fairer but each generation takes longer.

check.message: Call routesPerGeneration in the each generation block.

hints: The call takes a count of trips.

steps.title: New streets
steps.body:
A brain that only ever drives Midtown learns Midtown by heart. The benchmark drives two cities training never uses, so that habit costs it there.

`randomCity(seed: generation)` sends the next generation to a city built from the generation number, and `useCity` brings it back. Alternate them with `generation % 2`, which is 1 on odd generations and 0 on even ones.

check.message: Call randomCity in the each generation block.

hints: An if block runs its lines only when its condition holds: if generation % 2 == 1 { ... }.
Inside if generation % 2 == 1, write randomCity(seed: generation). Inside if generation % 2 == 0, write useCity(id: "midtown").
